Just as the four pillar bind, this surrounds the area, though this time it's a bit more solid. After creating a large, oven-like structure it then electrocutes the entire area inside, frying the contents and hopefully making it hard for them to escape.

Each Pillar has 300 HP and a DR of 20+CHA/5.
This is a Cube 25, inside a Cube 50, inside a Cube 75, inside a Cube 100; thus, it's 25 yards from the edge of one layer to the next. This may be defended with by dodging escaping 1 layer for every 4 points they beat the accuracy.
For each layer a person is inside they suffer -2 Immobilize and 1 Paralyze. If a Pillar is destroyed, that layer is forcibly ended. Thus, someone at the center would be at -8 Immobilize and Paralyze 4, until they managed to run 25 yards or destroy a pillar from one set; then they'd be at -6 Immobilize and Paralyze 3, and so forth.
This lasts so long as you maintain its upkeep. You are immune to its effects.

Harnessing a great amount of chakra, you create a field of lightning that swirls around you and coalesces into the crackling outline of an electric dragon. From there you can keep it at the ready, or attack an unfortunate foe immediately.

When you use this technique, you may choose to lower its Chakra cost by 10. If you do so, rather than launching at your opponents the lightning dragon takes shape coiling around you.
It will automatically attack the first person to move within 10 yards of you (it will not, however, trigger this effect if you move closer to them), with +4 Accuracy. You may also launch the dragon at any time while it's still around, as a Chakra 30 Speed 14 action.
Dense dark lightning sacrifices spread for brutal nervous-system pressure.

On a full hit, if the target already has Raiton-induced Paralysis, increase Wounding Damage by 10%.
After resolving, end 2 Severity of Raiton-induced Paralysis on the target as the built charge violently discharges.
A refined Chidori concentrates more of the current into a smaller, cleaner killing edge.

Requires Chidori. Ignore 25% DR and 25% Armor effectiveness.
After resolving, increase Chakra penalty by 2. This penalty is applied even if the Attack misses.

Upon completion of the handseals the user forms a ball of raw, condensed lightning chakra between their palms, then encases it in a more stable 'shell' made from hundreds of interwoven chakra strands, creating a mesh-like barrier that prevents the inner chakra from dissipating. After that, they can either leave the resulting ball of chakra hovering where it was made or hide it inside some appropriately sized physical object, typically the ground, where it will lie in wait until someone comes close enough to trigger the mine. When they do, it seeks them out and detonates on contact. If this is hidden inside some object, it cannot be detected without the use of a chakra-detecting doujutsu (such as Byakugan).

Set a range up to 60, whenever someone other than you enters this range, they immediately become the target of a Sneak Attack from this jutsu, using your ranks in Stalker, as the ball of lightning soars towards them without warning.
This can be left sitting in the air (as an effective deterrent), or submerged into any available surface (the floor, the walls). If you are within 60 Yards, you can prevent the ball from activating by concentrating on it (though you'd typically need line of sight to know if this is necessary).
Paralysis 6 for 50 ICs, This technique receives only half your damage bonus.

This technique truly earns its name. As the handseals are completed electricity will begin to arc along the user's body and wisps of dark smoke will rise from them, a result of the overwhelming, uncontainable amounts of chakra this jutsu requires.
That chakra is converted directly into electricity and released in a blast every bit as devastatingly powerful as a genuine bolt of lightning.

The effectiveness of partial defense is halved against this technique: for every 1 point it misses by, it deals only 10% less damage.
After rolling damage for Tenchu, you may spend a point of Willpower to reroll it and take the higher of the two results.
Rather than creating lightning from chakra, the user seizes control of a naturally charged storm and directs a true lightning strike down onto the battlefield.

Kirin uses natural lightning. It does not receive the normal NDB multiplied by Speed damage bonus; instead add NDB*10 to its damage.
The required thundercloud may be natural, or may be prepared by sending at least two B-rank or higher Katon techniques into open sky within the previous 100 IC. After Kirin resolves, the local electrical charge is spent; another Kirin cannot use the same setup.
Kirin cannot be parried by a technique below A-rank.

A deliberately tiny Suiton exercise: the user flicks a controlled burst of water with just enough force to drench a person, cool a surface, or put out something that was never meant to be a battlefield inferno.

Create roughly 1 gallon of clean water at the target point. This deals no damage. It extinguishes ordinary non-chakra flame in its Area and may remove 1 point of Ignite from a willing target, but cannot affect Burns or an Ignite created by a B-Rank or higher technique.
Mizudama no Jutsu - Water Sphere Technique
The user gathers the water used in this technique in front of them as they perform the handseals, and then directs it at an opponent as a high-speed projectile.

This is used alongside a Dodge Interrupt, and provides it with a +G bonus. After your first time using this in a Combat Encounter, your enemies begin to see it coming. Each time you wish to use it, make an opposed Espionage vs their Espionage, with a +5 for each time they’ve made this check this combat, on a success apply the effects as normal, on a failure you instead gain +G/2 to your dodge. Each time you fail for this combat the divisor of this increases by 1 (G/2, G/3, G/4, G/5…)
Suiton: Mizu Doka - Water Blending Technique

A thin film of chakra-laced water bends light around the user's outline and carries the colours of the surrounding terrain across their body. It is less perfect than true invisibility, but it works while moving and is especially effective in rain, mist, rivers, and wet terrain.

While maintained, gain +4 Stealth against checks that rely primarily on sight. If you are stationary in rain, mist, shallow water, or similarly wet terrain, this bonus increases to +6.
This technique does not conceal sound, scent, footprints, or chakra. Making an attack or using a damaging Jutsu ends the Upkeep after that action resolves.
Kirigakure no Jutsu - Hidden Mist Technique

This imposes a -G Visibility penalty to everyone in the Area as a supernaturally thick mist blankets the field. This mist is always centered on you.
While Maintaining this Upkeep you may recast at no Chakra cost with a G of your previous use. After you stop paying the upkeep, the mist's up penalty fades at a rate of 1 per 5 IC.

It was recently discovered that covering oneself in water is a highly effective countermeasure to being on fire! Thus, this technique: An alternative to the ever-popular "stop, drop, and roll", the ninja drenches themselves or a nearby object in water.
This reduces any Ignite penalties a target is suffering from by the amount of Gallons spent on this Technique.
Mizu Souzou no Jutsu - Water Creation Technique

You convert raw chakra into pure water. This technique is popular among serious users of suiton techniques, as it lets them avoid picking and choosing their battles so carefully, and allows them to eschew the practice of carrying around large gourds of water (which, in addition to giving away their specialty, are unpleasantly heavy).

You create X gallons of water. This may be used alongside a Jutsu with a Gallon cost. When used this way, add half X (rounded up) to that Jutsu's Chakra cost; Water Creation adds no Seal Speed and does not resolve as a separate action. It may also be used alone, in which case the created water is deposited on the battlefield or in a container you are wearing that has space for it.
Suiton: Namerakana Amamizu - Water Release: Rainwater Slick

The user splashes a small area with water, infusing it with their chakra. This layer of chakra causes the water to support a person's weight for just long enough that when it gives out, they'll risk slipping and falling embarrassingly. Anything coated in this is, similarly, hard to hold on to.

Make a Chakra Control roll when you first lay down this technique, with a +5 bonus.
Anyone who moves through this area by any means must choose to halve their speed or be forced to roll an Athletics check against that number. On a failure they become prone. This extends to determining penalties for AoE attacks. If they choose to move at full speed, they must make an Athletics Check against the same TN or fall Prone (though they still move the full amount). The Prone’s penalties do apply to any Defense against the Attack this was in response to.
Anybody inside the Area of Rainwater Slick suffers from Immobilization -1, as they have to put a little more thought into all of their actions.
The user condenses the water in the air to fire multiple blasts in unison. This allows for large crowd control or by focusing them into single targets it produces a much stronger attack.

You fire G number of projectiles and can direct them at a single target or split them between any number of targets. The X for this jutsu is determined by the number of projectiles thrown at each individual target.
Suiton: Teppoudama - Water Release: Liquid Bullet

The user kneads chakra and converts it into water inside their stomach, then spits it out in the form of a dense, chakra propelled ball. Its greatest boon to suiton users is that it can be used in an area without any preexisting water.
This adds 3 gallons of water to the battlefield every time it's used.
Takigakure Ryu, Mizukiri no Yaiba - Hidden Waterfall Style, Water-Cutting Blade

Originally developed by the Hidden Waterfall village, this technique has since spread into wider use. The first half of the name is generally dropped, though some choose to keep it out of respect. The jutsu creates a blade out of water, kept as strong as most metals by the chakra infusing it.

You craft a Sword upgrading it using X Artisan Points up to your Chakra Control - 4 + G/3. You may choose to double the Base Speed and Upkeep of this Technique to create a second Sword in your other hand during the activation of this Technique and both weapons gain the dual property.
The Sword (s) gains the following effects and Upgrades:
Its Sword lasts until you let go of it or end this Technique’s Upkeep
You may perform Handseals for Suiton jutsu by increasing the Seal Speed by 4 per weapon
The weapon has a third of its normal Durability
(2) Your weapon may add Gallons up to your ranks in this ability to the attack Its Damage Dice is increased by Gallons used * 5 . Max G (the G used in weapon creation)
A body of water formed around the user’s arms into long whip-like tendrils which can be used to grasp or strike an opponent or to intercept incoming attacks.

You may create X whips to a max of Chakra Control Ranks /5. The range of all taijutsu attacks is increased by 5 + X, but used in this way converts the attack into ranged and it gains knockback equal to half the range.
Mizu Bunshin no Jutsu - Water Clone Technique

An advanced form of the standard Bunshin no Jutsu, this creates clones out of water. Since they're solid (well, relatively) these clones can be used to perform tasks the user is unable or unwilling to do for themselves. While they're weaker than their user, they can still prove dangerous in combat.

You create X clones following all Bushin rules with the following exceptions:
A clone can be created with a Sword (From the Standard Equipment options) in hand by spending an additional 2 Gallons of Water on each clone. You may spend up to your Chakra Control - 5 Artisan Points on upgrading these swords, splitting it between all of your clones.
[1 AP] Dodge, or Parry.
[Variable AP] Move: The clone may move around the battlefield. This costs 1 AP per 2 IC it spends moving.
[Variable AP] The clone may make any basic unarmed or weapon attack, by paying 1 AP per 2 Speed of that action.
[5 + X AP] The clone can use itself to create a water prison (as per Suiton: Suirou no Jutsu) and on a success the clone is destroyed. X is the number of gallons for the jutsu’s cost and requires no actual gallons. You must pay the Chakra cost rather than the clones (though they still gain the upkeep. If you go to the prison you can take it over by assuming it’s upkeep, and from then on you are treated as having used the jutsu.
Mizugakure no Jutsu - Hidden in Water Technique
10 Gallons of Water on the field

The user sinks into a shallow pool of water, much too little to actually fit a person (it's ninja magic, don't ask questions), where they'll be able to easily lie in wait for a target to pass by, or spy on someone who might be near.

You hide, and immediately enter Stealth 3. If an opponent does not have a reason to suspect you're there (i.e. this isn't being done in-combat) you have a +5 Stealth bonus. You maintain awareness of your surroundings outside of the pool as if it's a window.
The puddle being reduced below 10 gallons, results in you being harmlessly ejected.
Mizutamari no Jutsu - Pool of Water Technique

A moderately advanced technique is the appropriately named water-walking technique; molding chakra below one's feet to 'stand' on patches of water without any actual expenditure of energy, and, once it's perfected, only minimal concentration. This technique builds upon that concept, creating a 'cushion' of static, almost-solid water beneath each foot that the ninja stands on to avoid direct contact with the ground.

You reduce any immobilization penalties due to the condition of the ground you're crossing by G, and ignore any other mechanical effects (such as damage for walking across caltrops) if they're C-rank or lower; if they're B-rank or above, you instead halve them. You are considered not directly in contact with the ground (for say, the Doton jutsu Shindou).
Suiton: Mizuame Nabara - Water Release: Syrup Capture Field
The user converts chakra into water, and infuses it with enough chakra to alter its composition, making it extremely viscous. They then spit it out in a stream of sticky, highly adhesive liquid.

If a person has the ability to walk on water, they may cross this area without difficulty. Anyone else in the area suffers a -4 immobilization penalty.
This jutsu's effects persist for 50 IC even after you drop the upkeep. However, so long as the upkeep is maintained, you may control the syrup enough to have it try to 'grab' anyone using water-walking to cross it unaffected; if the attack hits, the person is stuck in the syrup as if they weren't using water-walking. This is a Speed 6 action, with a Chakra cost of 15.
Suiton: Mizurappa - Water Release: Violent Water Wave

Inhaling a large amount of air and performing the necessary seals, the user will expel a copious amount of water from his/her mouth. The wave of water produced will slam against its opponent and can then be utilized for other techniques.
This technique adds 5 gallons of water to the battlefield every time it's used.
A vertical wall of water rises to catch an incoming attack and collapse around it.

Make a Ninjutsu Parry against a damaging Melee, Projectile, or AoE attack. On full success, protect only yourself unless the technique's Area explicitly fits behind the wall.
On success, add 10 gallons of water to your location after resolution. Against Raiton, suffer -2 to the Parry.
Suiton: Suikoudan - Water Release: Water Shark Blast

After creating the handseals, you launch water in projectile form at an opponent. Some ninja like to etch the outline of a shark's head into the end of this projectile; others, who believe that being a ninja is very serious business, prefer to omit that part of the technique. Experienced users can even use this to allow themselves to fly quickly through the water, while protecting themselves with the might of the tearing shark.
You may move to any location along the area of this technique, unhindered by anything which would normally prevent you from moving. You may ignore other Ground-Based effects during this movement.
Suiton: Suirou no Jutsu - Water Release: Water Prison Technique

The user gathers the chakra around their hand, and forms the required water into a sphere which encloses its victim. Due to the density of the chakra used in this technique, the water is stronger than steel. It is not, however, airtight. Yeah, don't ask how that works. We don't know either.

If this Jutsu hits, the victim is trapped inside a sphere of water. People inside cannot take actions, but they also cannot be affected by anything outside the prison; yes, that's right, the water can even stop giant swords. It makes sense, honestly, we promise, somehow. Anyone with a Chakra Control Rank of G*2 or above is able to mold the chakra around them to allow themselves to siphon air through the prison, meaning they can still talk and breathe. Any target with less CC, however, suffers a Suffocation 1 status every 10 IC. To maintain the water prison, you must keep one hand on it. Dodging requires you to end the effect; if you take damage, you must make a Chakra Control check against a TN of 5+(damage taken)/10 or the prison ends. Although you can't move, you can still take most other actions that are possible one-handed while maintaining the prison's upkeep.
Umi no Tate no Jutsu - Ocean Shield Technique

A derivative of a more advanced technique, this was created to help teach up-and-coming suiton users the foundations of that jutsu, and help keep them alive until they were skilled enough to learn it. It creates a circular barrier of water around you, which surges up to protect you from... well, whatever convinces you that you'd need to use this technique.

You may Parry a Melee, Ranged or AoE Attack with a Bonus of +(G/3). This works against jutsu weak to it up to A rank, jutsu strong against it up to C-rank, and all other Jutsu (including Taijutsu) up to B-rank.
Benzaiten no Jutsu - River Goddess Technique

Named after the deity who supposedly watches over a major river, this technique coats the user's body with a thin layer of chakra-infused water. It offers no real protection from impacts or weapons, but can be an effective supplement to one's defenses against heat and other unpleasantness.
You end any ongoing ignites on you. So long as this is maintained you cannot gain any by Ignite or Burn statuses, and you take (10+G)% less damage from Katon Jutsu (applied after other reductions).
Suiton: Bakusui Shouha - Water Release: Exploding Water Shockwave

The user creates an enormous amount of water by spewing it from their mouth, flooding the battlefield and potentially crushing foes in its path. Best of all, they get to look awesome while doing it! The wave rises up from beneath the user, and they can 'ride' it to its destination.

X is your ninjutsu damage bonus and produces that many gallons. This Technique's Speed cannot be reduced below 12 by any means and it cannot be Dodged unless you can completely escape the area.
As part of this technique, you may move up to half its Area in yards, in any direction. The Area of this Technique does not move with you - it remains centered on where your movement began.
Five chakra sharks move through water as a coordinated hunting pattern.

Requires the target to be touching a body of water containing at least 20 gallons. Make up to five attacks; divide the five damage groups among targets in the same connected water.
A target uses one Defensive Interrupt but rolls separately against each shark. Combine damage only for Wounding after all hits.
A thin, high-pressure stream turns water into a cutting tool.

Requires 8 gallons of available water or +5 Chakra to create it.
Against unattended objects and created Barriers, treat Damage as 25% higher. It does not bypass Armor or DR against creatures.
Suiton: Suigadan - Water Release: Water Fang Bullet

This move forms multiple pressurized, spiraling columns of water that have a drill-like ability to pierce and destroy their target. As this attack can originate from any body of water (rather than being shot directly from the attacker), in the right environments this has a 360 degree range of attack, making it incredibly difficult to defend against adequately.

If there are at least 10 Gallons of Water left in the Background after this Technique is used (or one is, say, over a lake, river, or other body of water such as Syrup Capture Field), this Technique is automatically a Surprise Attack.
Suiton: Suijinheki - Water Release: Water Encampment Wall
16 gallons of water or +8 chakra cost

This defensive technique creates a wall of water around you, which forms a violently churning defensive perimeter. When lacking water in the environment to use, a talented shinobi can form it in their stomach and spit it out.

If using Suijinheki as an interrupt: Roll a parry against the attack's accuracy, with a +6 bonus; if you succeed, this stops the attack entirely.
Once Suijinheki has been deployed, it lasts for your damage bonus in initiative counts--it automatically defends all attacks using your initial parry roll. It ends early if an attack breaks through the barrier or you may also end it early, if you need to move or attack through it.
This technique protects you and anyone within its area from any jutsu strong against this up to B-rank, and all other techniques (including taijutsu) up to A-rank.
A flat reflective water surface creates a momentary duplicate of an incoming attack's shape.

Use against a Projectile Ninjutsu up to B-rank. Make a Ninjutsu Parry at -2.
On success the attack is negated and the mirror breaks. If you beat the attack by 5+, the attacker suffers NDB×5 damage of the original technique's damage type; this reflected damage cannot Wound.
Suiton: Suiryuudan - Water Release: Water Dragon Blast

This technique shapes a large amount of water into a giant, dragon-shaped projectile which seeks out and crashes into whoever you direct it at. What it lacks for in complexity, it makes up for by being a highly effective tool in any Suiton using shinobi's arsenal.
Suiton: Takitsubo no Jutsu: Water Release: Waterfall Basin Technique

This technique drills a hole with existing water to an underground source of water and draws it forth, forming a geyser on the surface. The issue, however, as you may have guessed, is that you already need to have water on hand to make that hole, quite a bit in fact. Rocks tend to get quite tough to dig through once you reach the "Hidden sources of water" level. Gotta spend water to make water, just the way the world works, sorry. Aside from being useful for creating a spot to relax when resting or camping out, and ensuring you'll always have a source of clean water, it, like most ninjutsu, has combat applications.
This Technique adds (G/5) Gallons of Water onto the Background every 5 IC, for a Duration of 100 ICs.
Suiton: Uramiame - Water Release: Grudge Rain

As a weather-manipulation jutsu, this technique is extremely taxing upon its user. Upon its completion a large storm cloud is created, which proceeds to, as storm clouds are prone to do, rain. This rain saps the chakra from anyone it comes in contact with, and transfers it through the pooling water to the technique's user.

Every 10 IC, everyone other than the user and up to Chakra Control/5 people they've designated as allies has their Chakra Exhaustion penalty increased by 1, and the user has their Chakra Exhaustion penalty decreased by 1 per person present affected by the rain. If the user moves, they may cause the mist to 'follow' them; It moves at a speed of 0.5 Yards per IC until the user is back in its center.
Dai Bakusui Shouha - Great Exploding Water Shockwave
This technique receives only half your damage bonus.
A stronger but less directly offensive version of the B-rank Exploding Water Shockwave, the user spits out a truly prodigious amount of water.

This adds 40 Gallons of Water to the Background. So long as there are at least 30 Gallons in the Background at any time while this Technique's Upkeep is maintained, any Ground-Based Techniques (Such as Earth Split Turnaround Palm or Syrup Capture Field) become impossible to use. Regardless, all Suiton Techniques treat the maximum of their Gallons Requirement as if it was 5 higher.
Additionally, anyone who is standing in its Area will begin sinking even if they have the Water Walking Ability (The currents are simply too tumultuous). They can swim at half their normal movement speed (movement-increasing jutsu typically will not work), and until they've exited the area suffer Suffocation 1 every 15 IC. Alternatively, they can take a Speed 2 action to stay at the surface for the next 15 IC.
Suiton: Daibakufu - Water Release: Great Waterfall

This is one of the most powerful water ninjutsu in existence; once the appropriate seals are formed, the user unleashes a devastating tidal wave which tears across the battlefield like a scaled-down tsunami, knocking aside people, trees, and small buildings in its path.
Long ago, exceptionally skilled shinobi were able to fill their impromptu waterfall with all manner of weapons, which were propelled within the wave at incredible speeds. This had the effect of making it an almost inevitably deadly technique that would leave pools of blood mixed in with the water. However, use of that aspect of the technique was forbidden due to its unbelievable power, and as peace settled across the lands the secret of how to do that was lost.
This Technique pushes any targets hit with a Knockback of G.
Suiton: Daikoudan - Water Release: Great Shark Blast

This creates an enormous shark out of water and sends it crashing across the battlefield at whichever party has offended the user sufficiently for them to feel the need to do so. Aside from impacting its primary target, the shark is massive enough to cause significant collateral damage. The technique's true secret, however, is its ability to absorb any chakra it comes in contact with and use that energy to further empower itself.

As an interrupt this technique's Seal Speed is reduced by 10, its Chakra cost is increased by 10 and can only target the attacker.
Daikoudan may be used to Interrupt techniques so long as its Speed is equal to or less than theirs, but can only Interrupt Projectile Attacks. Compare the damage of these attacks with Jutsu weak to it reduced by 25%, and Jutsu strong against it increased by 25%. If the incoming attack does more damage, you are hit by it, but it has its damage reduced by your damage. If Daikoudan's damage is greater, it becomes an attack against the opponent with any Accuracy bonuses (but not penalties) of the attack it countered.
Similarly, if a ninjutsu-based defense is used against Daikoudan, and fails to stop it completely, it does full damage (bypassing even partial defense).
Suiton: Suiryuuben - Water Release: Water Hydra Whip

This jutsu creates a levitating orb of water which can project numerous whips and tendrils of water. These tendrils can be guided to targets by remote manipulation of the orb's chakra, even changing direction in mid-trajectory to find their targets. On top of that, they're sharp-tipped and more than capable of perforating opponents many times over.

When you first use this Technique, you create a levitating ball of water, and perform one Tendral Whipping Attack (mentioned below) for free. A So long as you maintain this technique, your pet giant levitating ball of water will fight for you! It acts 1 IC after it's created and can take the following Actions, by spending your AP:
[X AP, Speed X] Move: It moves as if it had taken a Speed (X)*5 action, using your CHA in place of its AGI. It cannot (deliberately) move outside its max range. If it does end up outside that range, it can take no actions other than moving towards you.
[3 + X*3 AP, Speed 12, Piercing] Tendril Whipping: You target X people within range. Your water ball makes a Projectile Attack against anyone within half this technique's max range, doing the above listed damage if it hits. This does piercing damage.
Additionally, the levitating water ball receives its own pool of AP equal to (G/2) which it may spend to perform the Action mentioned above and/or lower their own Speed.
This technique uses your base Accuracy at Fatigue 0 and half your NDB. Because the attacks are made by the technique, and not you, you cannot modify them further such as through Willpower or your own AP.
You hold the weapon high enough to threaten the first line immediately, accepting a more exposed defensive posture.
Your Chain 1 and Chain 2 Melee Bukijutsu gain +Athletics/5 Accuracy. Your Chain 3 Melee Bukijutsu gain +15% Final Damage.
The weapon stays low and close to the body, making it easier to receive an attack before committing to your own.

Gain +Athletics/5 to targeted Melee Parries. After fully defending against an enemy Attack, your next Melee Chain Attack against that enemy gains +15% Final Damage if it is your next non-Interrupt Action.
You extend the weapon into the space in front of you and make the opponent fight through its reach before they can reach your body.
Increase your Melee Weapon Reach by 50%, minimum +2 yards. Gain +Athletics/5 Parry against targeted Melee Attacks that began outside your unmodified weapon Reach.
You deliberately leave a line available, using the invitation to make the defender commit before your real angle is chosen.
After the target declares its Defense against your Chain Attack, impose a penalty of Athletics/5 on that Defense. The penalty applies once to each Attack, including one that generates multiple hits.
You keep the point or striking line fixed on one part of the opponent and sacrifice broader coverage for precision.
Reduce Called Shot Accuracy penalties with weapon attacks by Athletics/5, minimum 0. Called Shots gain +15% Wounding.
You build every movement around the next heavy commitment, gaining force at the cost of reacting cleanly when the opponent moves first.

Damaging Melee Bukijutsu gain +25% Wounding. Increase their printed Knockback by 50%, rounded down, and their printed Stun by half your PDB, rounded down. Apply these increases before Special rolls and Partial Defense.

A weapon on the ground is not “out of the fight”; it is a problem of distance, timing, and who reaches it first. You hook it with a foot, catch a returning cord, snatch it from the dirt, or draw a replacement without surrendering the exchange you already built.
Draw, pick up, or retrieve one weapon within arm’s reach without changing Chain value.

A practiced stance change should not look like somebody stopping to remember a new pose. You let the old guard collapse naturally into the new one, moving hands, feet, and weapon through positions that remain dangerous the entire time.

Switch from one active Bukijutsu Stance to another you know without changing Chain value. Pay this technique’s Stamina and Speed instead of the new Stance’s activation costs. The old Stance ends and the new Upkeep begins.

When an opponent trusts their weapon to catch yours, you punish the contact itself. The strike is allowed to bite into the defending edge, shaft, guard, or frame at the point of worst leverage, turning a successful defense into a durability problem.

Use retroactively after your weapon Attack is successfully Parried or Blocked by a weapon. After that Defense resolves, inflict WDP equal to half the defending weapon’s damage-level threshold, rounded up. Use that weapon’s Durability + its wielder’s DEX/10. This is explicit weapon damage and applies once to that weapon per Attack.

Chakra can make a weapon behave differently without changing what it physically is. You reinforce the part that matters for the injury you want—edge, point, striking face, or a projected chakra surface—letting one familiar weapon answer several kinds of protection.

Choose Blunt, Slashing, Piercing or Energy. One held weapon may deal that wound type and gains a Damage Bonus equal to half your NDB. Calculate this bonus when activating the technique, before bonuses granted by maintained weapon techniques.
Shaped chakra extends the weapon’s edge, point, or striking line beyond its physical reach, carrying the threat several yards past the material weapon.

One Melee Weapon gains additional Reach equal to the greater of its unmodified Reach or your CHA/5. When striking through this extension, it does not trigger on-contact punishment caused solely by touching the defender. Attacks still need a clear path.
You cut upward beneath the target’s guard.

On a full hit, note the Defense used. If the target uses that broad Defense against your next Sword Chain Attack, it takes a penalty of Athletics/5 and its final Speed is doubled when advancing its next action. This does not affect Interrupt validity.
You strike as the sword leaves its sheath.

Requires a sheathed sword. Reduce this Attack’s final Speed by 2 after modifiers, subject to normal minimums. If the target has not yet attacked you this combat, gain +25% Wounding. The sword ends drawn.
You bring the blade down through the opening made by your previous strike.

If your previous Chain attack was Chain 1, choose one when this Attack fully hits: Drop Weight — treat this Attack as 4 Speed higher for damage only; or Smother the Guard — note the Defense used against this Attack; that same broad Defense takes −Athletics/5 against your next Sword Chain attack.
You commit to a precise cut through the exposed target.

Gain +30% Wounding and reduce Called Shot penalties by Athletics/5, minimum 0. If your previous Sword Chain Attack hit through Partial Defense, use +50% Wounding instead. This exploits a weakened guard without requiring an already-broken Chain.
You change position while keeping your blade between you and the target.
Link to a Sword Attack. If the target Dodges, double that Defense’s final Speed when advancing its next action. This does not change whether the Defense is a valid Interrupt.
You draw and strike in one motion from a still stance.
Requires a sheathed sword. On the first use against a creature this combat, its Defensive Interrupts count as +2 Base Speed for Defense Validity. Ends drawn.
You reverse the blade across the line of your previous attack.
Read the Defense used against your previous Chain Attack. If the target repeats that broad Defense, it takes a penalty of Athletics/5. If it changes Defense, this Attack gains +25% Final Damage.
You turn the blade’s recovery into a second cut.
If the previous Chain Attack was partially defended, impose a penalty of Athletics/5 on the target’s Defense against this Attack.
You catch the attacking weapon and guide it aside.

Parry a targeted Melee Attack with +Athletics/5. On a full success, your next Sword Chain Attack against that attacker gains +Athletics/5 Accuracy if it is your next non-Interrupt Action. This does not defend against AoEs.
Chakra is run along the cutting geometry of the weapon, tightening the edge and keeping it from skidding or twisting on hard contact.

One sword gains +15% Wounding, stacking with its printed Sword Bukijutsu Wounding. Its edge may cut chakra-created physical bindings as an ordinary weapon Attack against that binding, using the binding’s normal durability and destruction rules. This grants no ability to cut intangible possession or effects without a physical target.
You shorten the sword and drive the point through a seam in the target’s protection.
Treat this Attack as Piercing. Reduce the target armor’s Absorption and flat DR by 25% for this Attack, after applying its damage-type matchup.
You feint with your shoulders and blade before striking along another line.

Oppose your chained target’s Awareness with Espionage. On success, its next Defense against your Sword Chain Attack takes a penalty equal to 2 plus 1 per full 5 points you won by, maximum 6. The opening ends when used or when the target completes its next non-Interrupt Action.
You sweep the blade from its sheath in a broad arc.
Attack every chosen enemy in the line with one Accuracy roll; divide Speed×PDB evenly among targets hit.
You draw your sword into the path of an incoming attack.

Requires a sheathed sword. Parry a targeted Melee Attack with +Athletics/5. On a full success, immediately make a Sword Basic Weapon Attack against the attacker at full damage if it is within Reach. The counter has its own Accuracy and Defense; its action time is included in this technique, and you pay the Basic Attack’s Stamina. End drawn. This does not defend against AoEs.
You sheath the sword quickly, readying another draw.

Sheathe one sword you hold without changing Chain value. If your next non-Interrupt Action is a Sword Chain 1, reduce its final Speed by 25%, rounded down, subject to normal Speed minimums, and gain +Athletics/5 Accuracy on that Attack.
You drive a decisive cut through the opponent’s exposed guard.

Gain +25% Final Damage and +25% Wounding. Choose Sever Guard or Carry Through when declaring. Sever Guard: if a weapon Blocks or Parries this Attack, after defense it suffers WDP equal to its damage-level threshold (Durability + wielder’s DEX/10), even if no damage reaches its wielder. Carry Through: on a full hit resolve Knockback equal to the greater of 10 or STR/3; on a successful Special, you may follow its actual movement, ending within Reach. These are explicit weapon damage and normal resisted Knockback respectively.
You catch the opposing weapon near its base and turn it aside.

Parry a targeted Melee Attack with +Athletics/5. On a full success, choose one: Turn the Line — win an Athletics Status Roll against Resistance to move the attacker up to STR/5 yards in any legal direction and apply Prone; or Seal the Line — the attacking weapon cannot Parry your next Sword Chain Attack if it is your next non-Interrupt Action. This does not defend against AoEs.
You drive the target back with a heavy strike.

Resolve Knockback using the greater of 3 or STR/10 as its printed severity. On a successful Special, choose to follow the target’s actual movement, ending within Reach, or increase the resulting distance by 50%. Obstacles stop movement normally.
You swing upward beneath the target’s guard.
Apply the printed Stun normally. If the target was already Stunned, replace this Stun with +20% Final Damage.
You strike into the opening left by the opponent's attack.
If this is your first non-Interrupt Action after resolving an Attack directed at you by the target, this Attack gains +Athletics/5 Accuracy.
You bring the weapon down on the target's head.
Make a Called Shot to the Head using its normal penalty. Gain +15% Wounding. There is no additional Accuracy or failed-Attack penalty.
You brace the club across the incoming blow.
Parry a Melee Attack with +2. On success, reduce Knockback from that Attack to 0. This does not defend against AoEs.
You sweep the weapon across several nearby opponents.
Attack all enemies in reach. Divide Speed×PDB evenly among targets hit. Resolve the Special separately against each fully hit target.
You strike the target’s ribs to disrupt their breathing and posture.

On a full hit, choose one: Smother the Breath — the target’s next Attack takes an Accuracy penalty of Athletics/5; or Rattle the Frame — apply Stun equal to the greater of 4 or half your PDB, rounded down. Smother the Breath ends after that Attack.
You direct the weapon’s weight into armour or a barrier.

After defense, deal this Attack’s damage directly to the struck armor piece, Barrier or Construct before resolving damage against its wearer. Apply structural damage-type matchups once. If that protection breaks, resolve the hit against the wearer without that protection; otherwise use its remaining protection normally. This structural strike is additional damage and does not bypass the target’s Defense.
Chakra and a shifted grip increase the weapon’s leverage.

One blunt weapon gains additional Reach equal to the greater of 2 yards or STR/10. Increase its printed Bukijutsu Knockback by 50%, rounded down, before the Status Roll. It may deal Blunt wounds even if another property would change its wound type.
You drive the club through the target’s base instead of through their centre, forcing them to choose between footing and impact.
On a full hit, choose Prone or Knockback equal to the greater of 6 or STR/5, then resolve the Special normally.
You adjust your grip to regain control of the heavy weapon.

For your next Club Chain Attack, halve temporary Accuracy penalties and weapon Delay, rounding the remaining values down. If neither applies, gain +15% Final Damage and you may treat it as Piercing by concentrating force into the weapon’s end. The benefit ends if your next non-Interrupt Action is not that Attack.
You strike a wall or defence with the weapon’s full weight.
Against Armor, Barriers and unattended objects, this Attack deals +45% final damage and cannot have its damage reduced below 50% by Partial Success.
You hit the defending weapon or limb hard enough to shake its hold.

If a weapon Blocks or Parries this Attack, it suffers WDP equal to its damage-level threshold after defense, even if its wielder takes no damage. It cannot Parry your next Club Chain Attack. Otherwise, a full hit applies Stun equal to the greater of 5 or your PDB, rounded down. This is explicit weapon damage.
You slam the weapon into the ground, sending an impact through nearby footing.

Strike the ground in an Area equal to the greater of 5 yards or STR/5, centered on you. Grounded enemies defend against your normal weapon Accuracy as an AoE; on a full hit, resolve Prone using Athletics against Resistance. No damage is dealt. Breakable ground becomes Rocky Terrain with severity equal to the greater of 2 or Athletics/10, maximum 5, until cleared or repaired. You are not affected by your own Prone effect.
You strike hard enough to send the opponent sprawling.

Use the greater of 12 or STR/3 as the printed Knockback. On a full hit, also apply Stun equal to the greater of 4 or your PDB, rounded down. Gain +25% Final Damage and +25% Wounding. No collision is required.
You charge through the enemy's position and drive them out of the fight's centre.

Use the greater of 12 or STR/3 as the printed Knockback. Before the Attack, use Move with an Attack in a straight line using its full final Speed instead of half. On a full hit, resolve Prone and Knockback with one Athletics Status Roll against Resistance. You may follow the target’s actual movement, ending within Reach. Obstacles stop movement without adding collision damage.
The thrust is carried through a passing step so the point threatens beyond the weapon’s usual measure.
Increase the weapon’s unmodified Reach by 50%, minimum +2 yards. On a full hit, the target cannot use Take the Hit until it completes its next non-Interrupt Action.
The rear of the weapon becomes a second striking end.

Treat the attack as Blunt. On a full hit, the target takes −2 to its next Attack against you before your next Action. On a successful Special, you may follow the target up to the distance it was moved, ending within your normal Reach.
The point is threaded through a small defensive window rather than swung around the guard.
Defensive Interrupts against this Attack count as +1 Base Speed for Defense Validity. Reduce the target armor’s flat DR by 20% for this Attack, after applying its damage-type matchup.
This is a committed line attack that spends the polearm’s reach aggressively.
Gain additional Reach equal to half the weapon’s unmodified Reach, minimum 2 yards, and +15% Wounding.
The user stops chasing the opponent and makes the opponent enter the weapon instead.
When a creature enters your Reach, make a Polearm Basic Weapon Attack at 85% final damage. It is Chain X.
The whole polearm is rotated through a controlled arc.
Attack all chosen enemies in Reach. If only one creature is targeted, gain +Athletics/5 Accuracy instead.
The hook, blade, or shaft catches posture instead of simply striking it.
On a full hit, choose one: Turn — resolve Knockback equal to the greater of 4 or STR/8 in any legal direction; or Sweep — resolve Prone normally.
You brace the haft and drive the point through the target’s line with enough commitment that the impact itself disrupts their movement.

This Attack deals Piercing wounds and gains +15% Wounding. Resolve Immobilization with severity equal to the greater of 2 or Athletics/10, maximum 6. It ends when the target spends a Speed 3 Utility Action to free the impaled clothing or equipment.
You catch the incoming strike and push the opponent out along the shaft.

Parry a targeted Melee Attack with +Athletics/5. On a full success, push the attacker directly away to any legal point within your Polearm Reach. This cannot pass through obstacles and does not defend against AoEs.
You hold the point forward and force approaching enemies to deal with it.

Increase Polearm Reach by 50%, minimum +2 yards. While maintained, when a perceived creature voluntarily moves from outside to inside that Reach, you may use Set Spear at full damage. A full hit stops that approach at contact. This does not stop teleportation or forced movement. Pay Set Spear’s normal costs and Interrupt Speed.
The head or shaft catches the opponent’s weapon and drags its line away from where they want to use it.

On a full hit, choose one held weapon. Until the target completes a Speed 3 Utility Action to free it, it cannot use that weapon to Attack or Parry. You must keep the Polearm in hand and the target within Reach; releasing the hook ends the restriction. You may continue Polearm Chain Attacks against that target while maintaining the hook.
You move around the opponent with the shaft between you and their weapon.

Link to a Polearm Attack against your chained target. If the target uses a weapon to Parry, halve that weapon’s positive Parry modifiers, rounded down. On a full hit, choose that weapon: it cannot Parry your next Polearm Chain Attack. Other legal defenses remain available.
The shaft is planted and used as a lever for the body.

Vault toward a target using Move with an Attack calculated from the Attack’s full final Speed. This movement may clear intervening difficult ground or a gap with a legal landing. On a full hit, resolve Prone using Athletics against Resistance. Against an already Prone target, gain +50% Wounding instead.
You catch the projectile on the shaft and turn it aside.

Parry a targeted Ranged Taijutsu or Projectile Attack with +Athletics/5. On a full success, redirect a physical projectile at its attacker if that attacker is within the projectile’s remaining Range. Use your Parry result as Accuracy and the projectile’s original damage; it defends normally. This counter adds no further cost or action time and cannot itself be redirected. This does not defend against AoEs.
You slide your grip to extend the point or put your weight behind the head.

Choose a benefit for your next non-Interrupt Action, which must be a Polearm Attack: Long Measure adds twice the weapon’s unmodified Reach; Short Measure gains +30% Final Damage and may attack at adjacency without the weapon’s minimum-Reach penalty. This does not remove other restrictions on using that weapon. Repeated uses do not stack.
You carry the thrust through the chained target and keep moving with it, using the opening to either pass their body or send the point into the next threat on the same line.

Gain +30% Wounding and ignore half the target armor’s Absorption and flat DR after its damage-type matchup. On a full hit, you may strike one creature directly behind it and within Reach at full damage. The second creature defends against the same Accuracy result. Resolve Chain progression once.
You catch the attack on the haft, drop your weight under it, and use the polearm as a lever to throw the attacker off their base.

Parry a targeted Melee Attack with +Athletics/5. On a full success, win one Athletics Status Roll against the attacker’s Resistance to apply Prone and Knockback equal to the greater of 10 or STR/3 in any legal direction. The throw may carry it beyond your Reach. This does not defend against AoEs.
The first gust is modest but highly controllable.

Resolve Knockback equal to the greater of 4 or CHA/10. On a successful Special, choose any legal direction. If this breaks the target’s Reach to a creature it was restraining, apply the restraint’s normal separation rules.
The fan snaps shut and is used like a short baton or edged frame.
Melee only. On a full hit, the target takes −Athletics/5 Parry against your next Fan Chain attack.
The fan snaps the current back toward you, pulling the target into a shorter and less comfortable distance.
Resolve Knockback using the greater of 3 or CHA/10; successful Knockback moves the target toward you rather than away.
The fan opens fully and the entire span contributes to one committed burst, driving a wall of air through the target hard enough to carry both body and guard with it.
Gain +15% Wounding. Use the greater of 5 or CHA/10 as the printed Knockback.
The fan catches a projectile in moving air instead of trying to meet it edge-on.

Parry a targeted Ranged Taijutsu or Projectile Attack with +Athletics/5. A full success also ends any effect carried solely by that projectile before it reaches you. This does not cancel an independent area effect or permit AoE defense.
The fan is used to claim a broad patch of battlefield with one sweep.
Attack all chosen enemies in Area. Speed×PDB is divided among targets hit. Resolve the Special separately against each fully hit target.
The current is turned across the target rather than straight through them.
Resolve Knockback equal to the greater of 4 or CHA/8 in any sideways direction. On a full hit, the target also takes a penalty of Athletics/5 on its next ranged Attack, consumed by that Attack.
The sweep is designed to clear a lane whether the attack connects cleanly or not.

Targets that fully Dodge move to the Area edge as part of that Defense. Targets hit suffer Visibility equal to the greater of 2 or Athletics/10, maximum 5, until they clear their eyes with a Speed 3 Utility Action. Apply Partial Defense to the severity normally.
Tiny changes in pressure, cloth, dust, hair, and projectile flight are read as information.

Make a Search using Chakra Control or Awareness with +Athletics/5. Your next Fan Attack against a creature located by this Search ignores Visibility penalties if it is your next non-Interrupt Action. It still requires a clear attack path.
The fan is held as a stable channel for both weapon pressure and Fuuton.
Increase the Range of Fan Bukijutsu and Fuuton cast through this fan by 50%. Increase their printed Knockback by 50%, rounded down, before Special rolls. These bonuses last while maintained.
The attack leaves a clean tailwind behind it, turning the space you just cut through into a lane for movement.

On a full hit, strip away the target’s maintained Prepare Blocking or equivalent Blocking stance. It must declare that stance again to regain its benefits. This does not end unrelated Upkeeps or cancel the Defense already resolved.
The user lets the fan pull their body through a short movement while preserving the chain.

Link to a Fan Attack. On a successful Knockback Special, you choose its direction. The target also becomes Prone using that same successful Status Roll. If the Attack has no Knockback, it gains Knockback equal to CHA/5, minimum 4.
The fan closes into a compact guard that can actually receive melee force.
Parry a targeted Melee Attack with +Athletics/5. On full success, your next Fan Chain 1 gains +20% Final Damage if it is your next non-Interrupt Action. This does not defend against AoEs.
The return current drags the target across your line while carrying you into the space their balance just abandoned.

Use the greater of 5 or CHA/5 as the printed Knockback. On a successful Special, choose any sideways direction and follow up to the target’s actual movement along a legal path. This follow replaces Move with an Attack for this technique.
The fan catches the rhythm of a Fuuton and carries it through the current exchange, allowing wind chakra to pass through the sequence without forcing the weapon flow to reset.

Once per Chain, your next Fan-tagged Fuuton used may be used without breaking Chain. It does not change or refresh Chain, and cannot trigger an effect that grants an additional weapon attack after using Fuuton.
You split the battlefield with one violent current and leave the air behind it too unstable for clean projectile fire.

Use the greater of 10 or CHA/3 as the printed Knockback. Gain +25% Final Damage. The Line remains turbulent until your next non-Interrupt Action; Ranged Taijutsu and Projectile Attacks crossing it take an Accuracy penalty of Athletics/5.
You shape a single clean current around an obstacle, letting the next attack arrive from a line the target cannot simply read from your stance.

Your next Fan Attack may bend up to twice, each by up to 90 degrees, within its total Range. Ignore Visibility penalties against targets you can locate and gain +25% Final Damage. Every segment needs a clear path. The benefit ends if your next non-Interrupt Action is not a Fan Attack.
The chain is cast past the target and tensioned back through them, so Range and pull are part of the same action.
Increase weapon Range by 25%, minimum +4 yards, for this Attack. On a full hit, initiate a Weapon Grapple and determine starting Control normally.
The lowest loop of the chain is used to attack footing rather than flesh.

On a full hit, you may deal 20% less final damage and initiate a Weapon Grapple. The target takes −Athletics/5 on the opposing Grapple check used to determine starting Control. While the Weapon Grapple remains a Clinch, the wrapped leg inflicts Immobilization 1.
The chain does not go slack after the first contact.

If the target is in your Weapon Grapple, this Attack gains Pummel and Trapping 2. On a successful Grapple roll, pull it toward you by up to half your current Control in yards, rounded down. If it cannot move because it is adjacent or anchored, gain +20% Final Damage instead.
The loop is placed high across the neck and shoulder line, where a small mistake becomes bleeding, shock, and a brutal loss of posture.

Called Shot to Head/Neck with its penalty reduced by 1. Apply Stun 2 normally. If the target is in your Weapon Grapple, this technique gains Takedown; on a successful Grapple roll, the target becomes Pinned by the Chain after the Attack resolves.
The chain is kept alive around the body like a moving perimeter.
While maintained, gain +Athletics/5 Parry against targeted Ranged Taijutsu and increase Chain weapon Range by 25%, minimum +3 yards. This grants no AoE Parry permission.
The chain sweeps across a lane instead of hunting one body.

Attack all chosen enemies in the line. Resolve the Knockback Special separately against each target hit; successful Knockback moves the target toward the centre of the Line rather than away from you. Wide Lash cannot initiate a Weapon Grapple.
Two lines of chain close around one limb.

If the target is in your Weapon Grapple, this technique gains Trapping 4. On a successful Grapple roll choose an arm or leg. Until the Weapon Grapple ends: arm = -2 Accuracy on actions requiring it; leg = Immobilization 2. Only one limb may be affected by Cross Snare from you at a time; a new application replaces the previous one.
The chain separates into several committed lines, each loop hunting a different limb or body as the user works the weapon across the field.

Requires the target to be in your Weapon Grapple. This technique gains Takedown. On a successful Grapple roll, the target becomes Pinned by the Chain and you may choose up to two limbs; each chosen arm takes −Athletics/5 Accuracy on actions requiring it and each chosen leg applies Immobilization 2 while the Pin remains.
Scenery becomes part of the weapon.

Anchor the chain around scenery or change its attack angle. Your next Chain attack or Weapon Grapple action may originate from the anchor for line of effect. That Attack or Grapple gains +Athletics/5 Accuracy.
The weapon is coiled into a defensive orbit close enough to parry melee attacks while still threatening at range.

Gain +Athletics/5 Parry against targeted Melee Attacks and increase Chain weapon Range by 50%, minimum +6 yards. After a full Parry against an attacker in Range, you may initiate a Weapon Grapple, resolving starting Control normally. The chain must be free to hold it; one Parry cannot establish multiple Grapples. This grants no AoE Parry permission.
The chain wraps a held weapon instead of the target’s body, turning their own reach and grip against them.

Requires the target to be in your Weapon Grapple. This technique gains Trapping 5. On a successful Grapple roll choose one held weapon and choose Attack or Parry; rolls of that type made with the snared weapon take -3 while the Weapon Grapple remains. At 8+ Control, the target cannot use that weapon for the chosen purpose until it successfully reduces your Control.
The user moves through their own slack instead of dragging the weapon behind them.

Link to a Chain Weapon Grapple action. If you win its Grapple roll, gain additional Control equal to Athletics/5. If you lose, halve the Control you would lose, rounded down. This cannot establish a Grapple without a legal initiating effect.
Tension is fixed to the environment and used as movement, leverage, or retrieval.

Attach the chain to a solid anchor within weapon Range and pull yourself to it, or pull an unattended object up to STR/5 weight units to you. Against a creature in your Weapon Grapple, instead win Grapple Offense against Grapple Defense to pull it up to half your Control in yards, minimum 5, toward you or the anchor. The chain must reach throughout; movement may be vertical.
The chain whips into the path of incoming fire and keeps moving after the deflection, carrying your footing with it.

Parry a targeted Ranged Taijutsu or Projectile Attack with +Athletics/5. On a full success, catch a physical projectile with the chain. If its attacker is in Chain Range and your chain is unoccupied, immediately initiate a Weapon Grapple against it using your Parry result as the attack Accuracy; it defends normally, then determine Control normally on a hit. This adds no further action time. This does not defend against AoEs.
This is the recovery skill that separates a chain fighter from somebody who merely owns a chain.

Use when your chain would be disarmed, dropped or knocked away. Keep hold of it; if already thrown, retrieve it from anywhere within its weapon Range along a clear path. Preventing loss of access preserves an existing Weapon Grapple. This does not prevent destruction of the chain.
You cast one loop around the target and another around the battlefield, then pull both lines tight until their movement is dictated by the anchor.

Requires the target to be Pinned by the Chain. This technique gains Submission and Control equal to the greater of 7 or Athletics/3. On a successful Grapple roll, choose a solid anchor within weapon Range and pull the target up to half your current Control in yards toward it. While maintained, the target takes a Dodge penalty of Athletics/5 and cannot voluntarily move farther from the anchor. Consecutive uses automatically hit as for a maintained Submission and apply Suffocation equal to the greater of 1 or half your PDB, rounded down. Destroying the anchor or ending the Weapon Grapple ends this technique.
You route the chain through several anchor points and turn the surrounding ground into a web of low, moving lines.

Connect up to 3 + Athletics/10 anchor points with your chain, all within weapon Range; the total routed length cannot exceed that Range. The field lasts until you retrieve the chain or a supporting anchor or chain segment is destroyed. When a creature crosses a line, resolve Grapple Offense against Grapple Defense. On success, apply Prone and initiate a Weapon Grapple with it, determining Control normally; the field ends as the chain tightens around that target. The same chain cannot simultaneously hold a creature and form this field.
Both weapons attack during the same entry, but they do not have to succeed together.
Make one Attack with each held weapon at 55% final damage each. Roll Accuracy separately. If either hits, Chain 1 is established.
The two weapons close like shears while the feet circle the target.

Requires two weapons. Choose one to attack and use the other to threaten the defender. If the target Parries, it takes a penalty of Athletics/5. If it Dodges, double that Defense’s final Speed when advancing its next action; Interrupt validity is unchanged.
The hands alternate in a broken rhythm, changing line and timing with every swing.

If this Attack uses a different leading weapon from your previous damaging Dual Chain Attack, gain +Athletics/5 Accuracy. Declare the leading weapon before the Defense; it supplies this Attack’s damage type and weapon properties.
The finisher commits both hands to the same exchange.

Make one Attack with each weapon at 65% Final Damage, rolling and defending separately. Combine successful hits for Wounding only. If both fully hit the same creature, resolve Prone using Athletics against Resistance. Resolve Chain progression once.
The off-hand weapon exists to solve the problems the leading weapon creates.

Parry a targeted Melee Attack with the off-hand weapon at +Athletics/5. On full success, your next Dual Chain Attack gains +15% Final Damage if it is your next non-Interrupt Action. This does not defend against AoEs.
The user turns both weapons through the surrounding space at once, each hand carving a separate line through the enemies close enough to be caught in the rotation.
Make one Accuracy roll with each weapon against every chosen enemy in Area; each successful weapon deals 50% final damage.
Each weapon asks a separate defensive question.

Make one Attack with each weapon at 60% final damage. The target chooses and resolves a Defense against each Attack. If it uses the same broad Defense against both, its second roll takes −Athletics/5. If it uses two different broad Defenses, each successful hit gains +2dS. Chain advances if either Attack hits.
You cross both attack lines through different parts of the target, forcing the defender to contain two wound lines at once before either hand can recover.

Requires two weapons. On a full hit, choose two different wound locations; if the Attack wounds, apply one wound at the normal location and a second wound one severity lower at the other location. The secondary wound cannot exceed Minor severity.
Two visible threats are used to split attention before the attack starts.
Oppose the target’s Awareness with Espionage. On success, choose Dodge or Parry; that Defense takes a penalty of 2 plus 1 per full 5 points you won by, maximum 6, against your next Dual Chain Attack.
The weapons settle into a shared rhythm, one hand recovering while the other remains live.

While wielding two weapons, gain +Athletics/5 Parry. When a Dual Chain Attack uses a different leading weapon from your previous Dual Chain Attack in the current Chain, reduce its final Speed by 20%, rounded down, subject to normal Speed minimums. Apply this once per Attack.
Each hand takes a different opponent, opening pressure on two fronts before the user decides which target to pursue.
Make one Attack with each weapon at 60% final damage. The attacks must target different creatures. If either hits, choose one hit creature as your chained target.
The style changes which weapon is “leading” without changing what is held.

Swap which held weapon is leading. Your next Dual Chain Attack may use either weapon’s damage type and ignores temporary Accuracy penalties specific to the other hand. If it is your next non-Interrupt Action, it also gains +15% Final Damage.
The two weapons close around the line the defender committed, trapping that weapon between them for the next exchange.
Requires two weapons. On a full hit, if the target used a weapon to Block or Parry, that weapon cannot be used to Block or Parry your next Dual Chain attack.
A full parry with one hand opens the line for the other.

After fully Parrying a targeted Melee Attack, make an off-hand Basic Weapon Attack against the attacker at full damage if it is within Reach. Pay this technique’s Stamina and Interrupt Speed instead of that Basic Attack’s costs. The counter has its own Accuracy and Defense and is Chain X.
One hand attacks the target while the other deliberately destroys the guard protecting them.

Requires two weapons. Make one Attack with each at full damage, rolling and defending separately. One strikes the target and gains +25% Wounding; the other strikes a held weapon or worn armor piece. Resolve that structural hit as a direct attack on the item, using normal item defenses and armor matchups. It does not also damage the wielder. Chain ends after both attacks resolve.
Each weapon carries a different chakra treatment, letting the pair answer two different defenses in the same exchange.

Maintain two different weapon-coating effects you know, one on each held weapon. Pay both activation costs and this technique’s Chakra cost. While maintained, pay this Upkeep plus only the higher coating Upkeep. Their effects apply to their respective weapons normally; ending Divergent Current ends both coatings unless their normal Upkeeps are paid.
The first arrow is used to establish a sightline rather than chase immediate damage.

Bow only. On a full hit, Mark the target until your Chain against it ends. Your next Bow Chain 2 against it gains +Athletics/5 Accuracy, increased by 1 if it voluntarily moved after being Marked. That Attack consumes the Mark. A new Mark replaces your previous one.
The arrow catches clothing or equipment, hampering the target’s movement.
Bow only. Resolve Immobilization with severity equal to the greater of 2 or Athletics/10, maximum 6. It ends when the target removes the arrow with a Speed 3 Utility Action.
You send the arrow toward an exposed angle in the defender’s guard.
If the target uses the same broad Defense it used against your Chain 1, that Defense takes −Athletics/5.
The bow is used as a platform for several distinct releases in one action.

Fire two arrows. Each uses the weapon dice plus this technique’s Damage dice; divide Speed×PDB evenly between them. Declare targets and roll Accuracy separately. Both may target your chained creature, or one may target a held weapon or worn armor piece on it using normal Called Shot penalties, item defenses and structural damage rules. Combine successful hits on the creature for Wounding only; item damage does not also damage its wielder.
You nock the next arrow in the same motion that lowers the bow, keeping the string, grip, and sightline ready before the target sees a reset.
Nock an arrow. Your next Bow Chain attack has -2 Speed, minimum Base Speed 3.
4 at a point within Bow Range
A high arc of arrows claims an area instead of one target, filling the space with descending shots and forcing everyone beneath it to find an answer at once.
Fire a volley; attack all chosen creatures in Area. Each target takes weapon damage with only 50% of Speed×PDB.
Two arrows share one draw and release timing but remain separate attacks.

Fire two arrows at the chained target, each at 60% Final Damage. Roll Accuracy separately; the defender declares one legal defensive method, pays its cost and Speed once, and rolls it separately against each arrow. If either fully hits and you know Marking Shot, establish or refresh your Bow Mark. Resolve Chain progression once; Partial Defense applies to each hit normally.
The final arrow is chosen for penetration and wound placement.

Gain +30% Wounding. Reduce the target armor’s Absorption and flat DR by 50% for this Attack, after its damage-type matchup. If the target has your Bow Mark, consume it when declaring to gain +Athletics/5 Accuracy.
An arrow is fired at another projectile rather than the attacker.
Consume an arrow to Parry a targeted Ranged Taijutsu or Projectile Attack with +Athletics/5. This does not defend against AoEs.
The bow is held in a disciplined firing posture, the sightline settling more firmly each moment the target remains predictable.
While maintained, Bow attacks gain +Athletics/5 Accuracy against targets that have not moved since your last action. If you move for any reason, you lose this bonus until your next action.
You place the arrow directly through one target’s line and keep enough force behind it to threaten the body standing behind them.

On a full hit, you may also attack one creature directly behind the target within the bow’s remaining Range for 60% Final Damage, using the same Accuracy result. It defends separately. The secondary hit cannot establish or advance Chain.
The draw is maintained through movement so the user can relocate without throwing away the shot, keeping shoulders, string, and target line stable while the feet change position.

Link to a Bow Attack. Move with that Attack using its full final Speed, in any legal direction. The movement does not remove Held Draw’s benefit for this Attack. If the target Dodges, double its Defense Speed when advancing its next action; Interrupt validity is unchanged. Bow only.
Chakra is fed into the ammunition as it leaves the bow, hardening the arrow’s flight and edge so it can bite cleanly into both flesh and chakra-made structures.
Ammunition fired from one bow counts as chakra-enhanced, gains +20% Wounding, and may damage chakra constructs normally.
The arrow is driven through gear or flesh and fixed into nearby terrain, turning a hit into a hard limit on where the target can go.

On a full hit, resolve Immobilization with severity equal to the greater of 3 or Athletics/10, maximum 6. If there is solid terrain within the target’s Reach, you may instead anchor it there; it cannot voluntarily move away until it removes the arrow as a Speed 5 Utility Action or destroys the anchor. The ordinary Immobilization ends when the target removes the arrow with that same Action.
You study the wind, the sightline and the target’s movement before drawing.

Make a Search with +Athletics/5 Awareness. Your next Bow Attack against a located target ignores Visibility penalties and gains +50% Range if it is your next non-Interrupt Action. The projectile still requires a clear path.
You send the arrow high above the target, then bring it down in a steep, plunging shot.

Choose a clear arcing projectile path within Bow Range and ignore Visibility penalties against a creature you can locate. Gain +25% Final Damage and +30% Wounding. On a full hit, resolve Prone using Athletics against Resistance. This adds no Delay beyond the weapon’s normal Bukijutsu Delay.
You settle into a firing lane and punish movement through it instead of waiting for a perfect stationary shot.

Choose a 90-degree arc within Bow Range. While maintained, when a creature voluntarily moves in that arc, you may make a Bow Basic Weapon Attack against it at full damage as an Offensive Interrupt. Pay that Basic Attack’s normal Stamina and final Speed. One movement Action can trigger one shot from you. The shot resolves at a point in its path that you can perceive and legally target.
Two compatible tools leave the hand on nearly the same line.

Throw two compatible weapons at one target and choose before its Defense: Crossed Blades — use one Accuracy roll and one Defense; each weapon contributes 55% of its damage, with its own damage type and legal payload, then apply that Defense’s result normally; or Decoy — one weapon deals no damage and distracts the guard, imposing an Athletics/5 penalty if the target Parries, while the other deals its full damage. Both weapons are spent; Chain advances once if the Attack hits.
A precise throw opens a bleeding cut or catches the target as it attacks.

Requires Kunai, Shuriken or Senbon. On a full hit choose one: Bleed — resolve Bleed equal to the greater of 2 or Athletics/10, maximum 6, using Athletics against Resistance; or Disrupt — the target takes an Accuracy penalty of Athletics/5 on its next Attack. Declare which projectile carries a poison or other payload before the Defense.
A tug on concealed wire sends the shuriken back toward its target.

Requires Ninja Wire for the entire clear projectile route. After the target fully defends, you may redirect the weapon along a clear return path within its remaining Range and force one repeat of that Defense. Reuse its paid Stamina, Chakra, AP and Speed; it pays and advances time only once. If the repeated Defense fails, resolve its ordinary Partial Defense against an Attack dealing 75% Final Damage. The repeated result replaces the first. Keep the wire committed until the Attack finishes; then you may retrieve the weapon along that route if it is not embedded or held.
Two fuuma shuriken cross the target’s path in quick succession.

Fuuma Shuriken only. Throw two weapons in succession, rolling and defending separately. Each hit deals 65% of weapon dice plus this technique’s Damage dice plus PDB × final Speed; combine damage for Wounding only. If both fully hit the same creature, resolve Prone using Athletics against Resistance as the crossing blades break its footing.
You spit a concealed senbon before the target sees you reach for a weapon.

Link to a Senbon Attack or Senbon Multi-Throw. Produce one concealed Senbon as part of the Attack without a Draw action; it counts toward normal ammunition and projectile limits. The first use against a creature that has not seen you use this trick is a Surprise Attack even if you were not Hidden. Other projectiles must already be readied normally.
The throw widens into a spread of tools that blankets an area, the user fanning their release so several targets are threatened by the same handful.

Supply one thrown weapon per chosen creature in Area, within your normal Multi-Throw allowance. Make one Accuracy roll; each target defends separately and can be hit by one weapon. Each fully hit target takes an Accuracy penalty of Athletics/5 on its next Ranged Attack. Pay normal ammunition and add this technique’s Stamina to the normal Multi-Throw Stamina, using this technique’s printed Speed.
You bounce the weapon off a hard surface or another projectile to strike from a new angle.

Choose a bank point along a clear route within total throwing Range. Use a hard surface, or throw an additional compatible weapon to create the ricochet point; that extra weapon counts toward your Multi-Throw limit and costs its normal Multi-Throw increments but deals no damage. Measure the Attack’s final approach from the bank point and reduce Visibility penalties by Athletics/5. Both segments must be clear. This changes the attack angle without automatically granting Surprise.
The user empties a full handful in one practiced release, splitting the weapons between targets as the throw opens across the battlefield.

Multi-throw up to Athletics/5 additional weapons beyond your normal allowance, splitting them among legal targets. Use normal Multi-Throw damage and costs; distribute this technique’s extra dice once per target across its projectiles. Each target defends separately. Against a creature fully hit by at least two projectiles, you may resolve Immobilization equal to Athletics/5 using Athletics against Resistance, pinning its clothing or equipment. It can remove this Immobilization with a Speed 3 Utility Action.
You draw your scattered weapons back into your hands with a sweep of chakra.

After your Thrown Attack resolves, recover its missed or deflected weapons along clear return paths within normal throwing Range. Weapons embedded in a creature, held by someone else, destroyed or consumed cannot be recovered this way. The recovered weapons are ready in your hands or carried holders; recovering them does not grant another Attack.
Years of throwing have stripped wasted motion from the draw, grip, and release.

Halve the Speed added by Multi-Throw, rounding the remaining added Speed up, and increase its weapon allowance by Athletics/5. Use the highest extra allowance granted by Bukijutsu, not their sum. Normal Speed minimums and ammunition costs still apply.
You split the throw across two opponents, using separate lines so neither target can read the whole release from one hand motion.

Throw one compatible weapon at each of two creatures at 60% Final Damage, rolling and defending separately. You may use this at Chain 0, 1 or 2. If the original chained target is hit, you may preserve your current Chain value against it. Alternatively, choose a hit creature and begin a new Chain 1 against it, ending the previous Chain and any unused Opening. This does not maintain two Chains or advance a preserved Chain.
Ninja Wire is attached or routed before the next throw so the projectile can travel farther and turn a corner the hand alone could not produce.

Route Ninja Wire from your hand or a thrown weapon you have already placed along a clear path. Your next Thrown Chain Attack gains +50% Range and may turn up to 90 degrees along that route. Supply wire for the entire route; it cannot pass through solid barriers. You may keep a placed weapon as the anchor for later uses, but each Attack needs its own use of Corner Wire. Cutting, detaching or retrieving the wire ends the setup.
You fix the payload to the projectile as you prepare the throw.

Link to a Thrown Attack. As part of readying it, apply up to two compatible attachments to one projectile, such as a paper tag, wire loop or poison coating. Pay their normal item and resource costs and make required application checks; this Link replaces preparation actions, not separate activation or detonation actions. Follow normal payload compatibility and stacking rules. No payload is copied onto other projectiles.
The weapon continues through its first line and curves toward a second target before it loses momentum.

After the first strike resolves, direct the weapon along a clear path within its remaining Range. Choose another creature, or the original target only if it fully defended the first strike. Make a new Accuracy roll; the target defends normally against 80% Final Damage. This Attack cannot also force a Defense reroll. Resolve Chain progression once against the original chained target. If neither strike leaves the weapon embedded or held, it returns to your hand along a clear remaining route.
You spread a prepared handful across the target’s guard, choosing which tools carry the real threat.

Link to a Multi-Throw. Gain +Athletics/5 Accuracy and up to Athletics/5 additional weapons; use the highest extra allowance granted by Bukijutsu. Pay normal ammunition and Multi-Throw costs. A creature fully hit by at least two projectiles suffers Bleed equal to Athletics/5 after a successful Athletics Status Roll against Resistance, once per target. Choose ammunition types and payloads when declaring, not after Defense.
You send a Fuuma Shuriken through a continuous cutting route, forcing several targets to solve the same spinning weapon from different angles.

Fuuma Shuriken only. Choose up to 3 + Athletics/10 creatures or exposed mundane bindings along one continuous clear path within Range.
